What it does: How far from the camera copies are drawn, in units. Over the last fifth of that distance, copies thin out a few at a time, so far foliage fades instead of ending in a line.

A simpler version of the asset: a model (.glb or .gltf) or a picture (.png or .jpg), which is drawn as a flat card. Press Choose... under the field to pick the file, or type its path, which is relative to the foliage list's file. Empty the field to stop using the level. If the file can't be found, the asset's own model is used.
The distance from the camera from which the level is used. Give later levels larger distances, such as 40 for level 1 and 100 for level 2. A new level starts at half the draw distance.
How far before a level's distance the change begins, in units. At 0, a cell switches all at once. At 10, a growing share of the copies switch over those 10 units, so the change is hard to notice.
